blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in Algonquin Homes
blocks.intro: Algonquin's newer homes have their own freeze points.

items.body: A bathroom or bedroom over a garage has pipes in a floor that sits over unheated space.
Kitchen and laundry lines on outside walls freeze in a deep cold snap.
A hose left on or a sprinkler backflow not drained can split.

items.h3: Homes Left Empty Over the Holidays
items.body: Turning the heat down too far while you're away is a common cause.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: How do I thaw a frozen pipe safely?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe slowly. No flames.
items.answer: Open the faucet, then warm the pipe slowly with a hair dryer or space heater, starting near the faucet. Never use a torch. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: How do I protect pipes over my garage?
items.preview: Keep the garage door closed and the house warm, and insulate the floor.
items.answer: Keep the garage door closed in cold weather, keep the house heat up and make sure the floor over the garage is insulated. We can insulate or reroute problem lines.

items.q: Should I drain my sprinkler system?
items.preview: Yes, before the first hard freeze.
items.answer: Yes. Have the system blown out before the first hard freeze so the backflow device and lines don't split.

items.q: Why did my pipe leak after it warmed up?
items.answer: The pipe split while it was frozen. Water only escapes once it thaws.

items.q: What does burst pipe repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on location and access. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on where the break is, the pipe and access. We quote a flat rate before we start.
